title: Uniform finite-time vanishing-viscosity convergence for Lipschitz aggregation potentials with well-prepared probability data
source_title: Vanishing viscosity limit for aggregation-diffusion equations
author: Frédéric Lagoutière; Filippo Santambrogio; Sébastien Tran Tien
difficulty_reason: Weak compactness alone does not identify the nonlinear interaction force when mass concentrates at atoms and the Lipschitz potential has a nondifferentiable diagonal. The authors symmetrize that interaction, pass both dissipative terms through the viscosity limit and use equality in the limiting energy inequality to recover the exact velocity field with zero diagonal convention. This new nonlinear measure-level identification closes the aggregation equation, beyond the standard Wasserstein compactness or gradient-flow foundations.

historical_source_pdf_evidence.original_difficulty_reason: The authors pass every dissipation term through the vanishing-viscosity limit, use a symmetrized interaction to resolve discontinuous forces at concentrating atoms and recover the exact diagonal-zero velocity from equality in the limiting dissipation inequality. This measure-valued nonlinear limit exceeds qualifying-exam PDE compactness.
